payload.question: On the NASA Exoplanet Archive TESS TOI table, does evaluating a vetting classifier only on resolved TOIs overstate its accuracy on candidates that look like the unresolved pool, and should resolved-set AUC be corrected before it is quoted as triage accuracy? This is studied in a semi-synthetic simulation: labeled TOIs (CP vs FP+FA) are re-split, host by host, into a pseudo-resolved set and a pseudo-unresolved set using a resolution model fitted to the current catalog, so the true accuracy on the pseudo-unresolved set is known.

payload.claim: AI-generated, untested hypothesis: In semi-synthetic splits of labeled TESS TOIs (CP vs FP+FA) using a catalog-fitted resolution model with selection strength gamma, the naive resolved-set AUC overstates true AUC on the pseudo-unresolved set. The gap grows with gamma. Importance-weighted estimators (iw, iw_clip) shrink the gap relative to naive. Clipped IW gives the best bias-variance tradeoff at gamma=2. Among the options, hgb_iw_clip is the most likely to be the best-supported correction.
payload.falsifier: (a) At gamma=2 the naive gap is below 0.02 for both lr and hgb, with range including 0 (supports no_correction). (b) The gap at gamma=0 is at least 0.02 (pipeline artifact). (c) At gamma=2 iw or iw_clip is no closer to zero than naive. (d) lr_iw_clip beats hgb_iw_clip, or unclipped iw beats clipped iw, on abs error.
payload.prediction: Over 20 host-level splits per cell, at gamma=0 the mean gap is below 0.02 in absolute value for every model and estimator. At gamma=2 the mean naive gap is at least 0.02 for at least one model, with a 95% range that excludes 0. The mean absolute error for iw_clip is at least 0.01 lower than for naive. At gamma=2 the best iw_clip arm has mean abs error below 0.02, and hgb_iw_clip has the smallest.

payload.falsifier: hgb naive gap at gamma=2 below 0.02 (and lr naive gap also below 0.02), which would mean no_correction. Other falsifiers: gamma=0 gap >=0.02; iw no closer than naive; lr_iw_clip beats hgb_iw_clip.

candidates.design: hgb, naive estimator, gamma=2, seed 2. Highest-bias condition for the flexible model.

payload.rationale: E1 has the highest eig/cost. Novelty check not run; results preliminary.
